result.evidence:
In src/ingest/parser.ts, text.split("
") splits files into lines. When a file ends with an empty line (or trailing newline), the last element in lines is an empty string (""). Although parser.ts has `if (lines.length > 0 && lines[lines.length - 1] === "") lines.pop();`, if the file ends with a blank line (i.e. two newlines at the end, or Windows CRLF line endings resulting in trailing carriage returns ``), the last element in `lines` is not `""` (it might be `""` or a blank line with whitespace, or if there's a blank line at the end of the file, `lines.pop()` removes the empty line produced by the trailing newline, but leaves the actual blank line preceding it as a data row). Specifically, if a file ends with a blank line (e.g. `...transaction

`), splitting by `
` produces `...transaction`, `""`. `lines.pop()` removes the last `""` (caused by the final newline), leaving `...transaction
` as the last line in `lines`, which is an empty line (or if the file has `
`, `lines` contains ``). Wait, let's trace:
If input is `"date,amount,description
2026-03-01,1,x

"`:
`text.split("
")` gives `["date,amount,description", "2026-03-01,1,x", "", ""]`.
`lines.pop()` removes the last `""` (from the trailing newline).
`lines` becomes `["date,amount,description", "2026-03-01,1,x", ""]`.
The loop processes `lines[2]`, which is `""`.
`splitFields("")` returns `[""]`.
`assertShape([""], header, 2)` checks `[""].length !== header.length` (1 !== 3), throwing `IngestError("errors.rowShape", { row: 3 })`.
Thus, a blank line at the end of the file (or files ending with `

`) is treated as a data row, leading to a 'Malformed row' error at the row just past the last transaction.

input.title: Handle trailing blank lines and carriage returns in parser
input.body:
File: src/ingest/parser.ts

Trim trailing whitespace and carriage returns from lines or filter out empty/whitespace-only trailing lines when parsing ingested files, preventing trailing blank lines from being treated as malformed data rows.
